newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev ends touch softer at 768-770 to dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev ends touch softer at 768-770 to dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 768-770 per dollar, a touch softer from its opening at 760-770 and down from 745-750 at the previous close due to insufficient foreign currency supply, dealers said.

"The lev was under pressure because a dollar purchase order from an oil importer near 770 had to be serviced by a market that has been generally reluctant to offer foreign currency amid the current political instability," said a dealer.
Dealers also said that interbank volumes were light due to low foreign currency supply amid expectations of a further lev depreciation.

A lev fall on the cash market to 755-770 from 720-730 on Monday also added pressure on the local currency in interbank trade, traders said. The dollar was offered at 790-800 levs at some exchange bureaus in the late afternoon.
The lev was likely to weaken beyond 800 per dollar on the interbank market by the end of the week in the absence of central bank support, traders said.

The central bank has said that pending payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt would be a priority and has refrained from interventions after its foreign exchange reserves fell to $518 million at end-December.
Next week Bulgaria has to pay some $135 million coupon on its Brady bonds out of a total of $300 million foreign debt payments due in the first quarter. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
